- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price has recently dipped.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in next period; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is significantly higher than recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias and reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.0s), model may overfit to recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.0/1.0), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use smoother moving average or reduce forecast variance.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply lagged sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day average) to dampen overcorrection.
